patients.summary: Healthy graduate student and distance runner who joined the practice at 21. In 2025 she had a right second metatarsal stress fracture, then a right distal tibial stress fracture, then mild accidental hypothermia at a December marathon finish; all resolved.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
21 yo woman here as a new patient. Grad student, just started her program this fall. Last primary care was her pediatric/adolescent practice; she has not had a physical in about two years. No complaints today.

PMH: none. No hospitalizations, no surgeries.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: nothing significant that she knows of.
SH: never smoker, does not drink, no drug use. Runs most days, mostly 3-6 miles, has done a few local road races. Lives in an apartment in Chicopee.
Gyn: menses regular.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: vitals as charted, BMI normal. Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT clear, TMs normal. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no adenopathy. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Ext: no edema, full ROM. Skin: no rashes, no concerning lesions. Neuro grossly nonfocal. Mood good, affect bright.

PHQ-9 2, GAD-7 3.

A/P: Healthy young adult, establishing care.
- Baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH today.
- One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening today, she agrees.
- Records request to prior office for immunizations. She thinks she finished HPV.
- Pap due now that she is 21, she would rather do it at a separate visit; plan at next physical.
- Flu shot when available, nurse visit.
- Return yearly, sooner as needed.

Immunization record: routine childhood and adolescent series complete. Entered here: Tdap 06/20/2013; HPV 9-valent 06/20/2013 and 01/09/2014 (two-dose series complete). COVID-19 Pfizer-BioNTech 04/17/2021 and 05/08/2021.

Visit notes: well visits through age 19, normal growth and development, no chronic problems, no medications, no known drug allergies. Sports physicals for cross-country.

Reviewed by PCP; immunizations entered.

orders.reason: right foot pain in a runner, possible stress injury

documents.title: Office Visit — Right Foot Pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Texted yesterday about her right foot, seen today. About a week of pain on top of the right forefoot/midfoot. Started a more intense training block a couple of weeks ago, running several miles every day. No fall, no twist, nothing she can point to. Hurts more the longer she runs and on stairs, better when she rests it. Has been taking OTC ibuprofen, says it barely touches it.

No meds otherwise. NKDA.

O: Vitals as charted. Walks without a limp. R foot: no swelling, no bruising, skin normal. Tender over the shaft of the 2nd metatarsal, the rest of the forefoot and the ankle nontender. Full ankle and toe ROM. Pulses normal, sensation intact.

A/P: R foot pain in a runner after a jump in volume, focal 2nd metatarsal tenderness. Worried about a stress injury.
- Referral to sports medicine, they have a slot next week and can image there.
- No running until she's seen. Bike or pool is fine if it doesn't hurt.
- Supportive shoes, no barefoot walking.

conditions.label: Stress fracture of right second metatarsal

reports.text: RIGHT FOOT, 3 VIEWS. Indication: right forefoot pain in a runner. Findings: No fracture line, periosteal reaction or cortical irregularity. Metatarsals and phalanges intact. Joint spaces preserved and alignment normal. Soft tissues unremarkable.

documents.title: Sports Medicine Consultation
documents.author: sports medicine
documents.body:
Outside Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Date of service: 06/11/2025
Re: Megan Foster, DOB 05/13/2001

Thank you for referring Ms. Foster, a 24-year-old graduate student and distance runner, for evaluation of right foot pain.

History: Two weeks of worsening right foot pain. It came on soon after she began a demanding training plan that has her running multiple miles every day. She recalls no injury. Activity brings it on and rest eases it. Over-the-counter ibuprofen has helped very little. Otherwise healthy, takes no other medications. No known drug allergies. No significant family history. Never smoker, does not drink.

Examination: The midfoot is tender to palpation, maximal over the second metatarsal. No swelling, redness or warmth. Neurovascularly intact.

Imaging: Three views of the right foot obtained in clinic, read as normal.

Assessment: Right second metatarsal stress fracture, diagnosed clinically. Plain films are frequently negative this early, and her point tenderness and history are typical.

Plan:
1. No running for about 6 weeks. Non-impact cross-training (cycling, pool running) as tolerated without pain.
2. Stiff-soled shoe for daily walking; walking boot provided for use as needed if walking is painful.
3. Acetaminophen for pain as needed; we suggested she avoid ibuprofen while this heals.
4. Follow up here in about 5 weeks to assess return to running.

Allergies: NKDA.

Please call with any questions.
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine

documents.title: Boot Question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, sports med said it's a stress fracture in my foot. Do I really need the boot to walk to campus? The stiff shoes seem ok. And is tylenol fine to take with nothing else?

documents.title: RE: Boot Question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I got their letter. Their plan was the boot only if walking hurts, so if you're comfortable in the stiff shoes that's fine. Acetaminophen is fine, up to 1000 mg at a time and no more than 3000 mg a day. Hang in there with the no-running part, it matters most.

documents.title: Sports Medicine Follow-up
documents.author: sports medicine
documents.body:
Outside Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Date of service: 07/16/2025
Re: Megan Foster, DOB 05/13/2001

Follow-up of right second metatarsal stress fracture, five weeks out. She held off running and has been cycling. Walking without pain for the past two weeks; stopped the boot early. No medications. NKDA.

Exam: No tenderness along the second metatarsal or elsewhere in the forefoot. No swelling. Pain-free single-leg hop on the right.

Assessment: Healed clinically.

Plan: Gradual return to running, starting with walk-run intervals every other day and building mileage slowly over 4 to 6 weeks. Back off if pain returns. Follow up as needed.

Orthopedics & Sports Medicine

reports.text: RIGHT TIBIA AND FIBULA, 2 VIEWS. Indication: distal right shin pain in a runner. Findings: No acute fracture or dislocation. Cortices smooth without periosteal reaction. Ankle and knee joints aligned. Soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: No acute fracture or dislocation of the right tibia or fibula.

documents.title: Sports Medicine Consultation
documents.author: sports medicine
documents.body:
Outside Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Date of service: 11/12/2025
Re: Megan Foster, DOB 05/13/2001

Ms. Foster is back with us five months after we saw her for right foot pain, this time for three weeks of right shin pain. It started after she lengthened her runs ahead of a marathon she has coming up. Running makes it worse, rest makes it better. No falls or other injury. No medications. NKDA. Past history notable for a right second metatarsal stress fracture this June, healed.

Examination: The distal third of the right tibia is mildly swollen, with a focal spot that is tender on palpation. Skin is not red or warm. Ankle moves through a full, normal range.

Imaging: Two views of the right tibia and fibula today show no acute fracture or dislocation.

Assessment: Right distal tibial stress fracture, a clinical diagnosis with negative early films. Second bone stress injury this year.

Plan:
1. No running for 6 to 8 weeks. Low-impact cross-training as long as it is pain-free.
2. Walking boot if walking is painful.
3. We recommended she withdraw from the upcoming marathon; she was disappointed and said she would think about it.
4. Follow up in about 8 weeks.

Thank you for the referral.
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine

events.reason: Collapse and confusion at marathon finish

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit date: 12/07/2025, arrival 13:05
Patient: Megan Foster, 24F, DOB 05/13/2001

CC: Collapsed after crossing the marathon finish, confused.

HPI: 24 yo female runner brought from the race medical tent after collapsing at the finish line. On arrival she is shivering, disoriented and her speech is slurred. Friends with her say she was dressed sensibly for the weather but was clearly having a hard time over the final miles. History of right metatarsal and right tibial stress fractures. Takes no medications. NKDA.

Triage vitals: T 34.5 C (94.1 F), HR 58, BP 100/60, RR 16, SpO2 98% RA.

Exam: Skin cold to touch, extremities pale. Cap refill 3 sec. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen soft. No signs of trauma. Moves all extremities. Remainder of exam unremarkable.

Labs: Na 140, K 4.2, Cr 0.9, glucose 90. CBC within normal limits.

ED course: Wet race clothing removed, warm blankets and forced-air warming blanket applied, 1 L warmed normal saline IV. Shivering eased over the first hour. At 2 h T 35.9 C, HR 66, BP 106/64, now answering questions appropriately. At 4 h T 36.8 C, HR 72, BP 112/70, RR 14, SpO2 99%, alert and oriented x3, speech clear, tolerating fluids by mouth, walking steadily.

Impression: Accidental hypothermia, mild, after marathon. Rewarmed.

Disposition: Discharged home 17:35 with friends. Warm fluids, rest, and avoid running until cleared. Return for confusion, fainting, or chest pain. Follow up with primary care this week.

Emergency Medicine

events.reason: Follow-up right distal tibial stress fracture

documents.title: Sports Medicine Follow-up
documents.author: sports medicine
documents.body:
Outside Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Date of service: 01/14/2026
Re: Megan Foster, DOB 05/13/2001

Follow-up of right distal tibial stress fracture, about 9 weeks from diagnosis. She ran the December marathon and was treated in an ED afterward for hypothermia, now recovered. No running since then; cycling and swimming. Walking without pain. No medications. NKDA.

Exam: Distal right tibia nontender, no swelling. Pain-free single-leg hop on the right. Ankle and knee normal.

Assessment: Healed clinically.

Plan: Graded walk-run return over the next several weeks, mileage increased slowly, no more than one hard change per week. Stop and contact us if bone pain returns. Follow up as needed.

Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
